newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK businessman seen lobbying for top post-97 job.
newsitem.headline: HK businessman seen lobbying for top post-97 job.

text.p: Hong Kong businessman Peter Woo has launched a low-key campaign to run for the position of the territory's first chief executive, newspapers reported on Saturday.

Woo, chairman of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd and a member of a China-appointed body preparing for the handover next year, had disclosed to leaders of some political parties his intention to run for the top post, the South China Morning Post reported.
The son-in-law of late shipping tycoon Sir Yue-kong Pao, Woo is also chairman of the Hospital Authority.
Woo, who has not made any official announcement, was not immediately available for comment.
Hong Kong, a British colony of 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997 and has so far seen only two candidates committing themselves to run for the top job.
But public opinion polls put Governor Chris Patten's deputy Anson Chan far ahead of the field. She has not officially declared her interest.
Declared candidate, former Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang ranks second in the popularity stakes ahead of Lo Tak-shing, a solicitor and the first to state his interest.
Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, widely tipped as a Beijing favourite, told reporters last week he would make a decision soon on whether he would enter the race.
